That single fact solves most polygon questions.","key_concepts":["Interior and exterior angles at a vertex add to 180 degrees","The exterior angles of any polygon sum to 360 degrees","In a regular polygon all exterior angles are equal"],"formulas":[{"note":"n is the number of sides.","label":"Interior angle sum","expression":"(n - 2) x 180 degrees"},{"note":"Rearranges to n = 360 / exterior angle.","label":"Regular polygon exterior angle","expression":"360 / n degrees"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Let the angles be 5x and 4x","They sum to 180, so 9x = 180 and x = 20","Exterior angle = 4 x 20 = 80 degrees","n = 360 / 80 = 4.5, which is not a whole number"],"answer":"The number of sides is not an integer, so the polygon cannot exist.","question":"A regular polygon has interior to exterior angle ratio 5:4. Explain why this is impossible."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"That formula gives the total. Find the alternate angle and the co-interior angle."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Corresponding angles form an F shape; alternate angles form a Z shape.","mistake":"Calling equal angles corresponding when they are actually alternate."},{"fix":"They add to 180 degrees, and are only equal when both are 90 degrees.","mistake":"Assuming co-interior angles are equal."},{"fix":"Look for the arrow markings. Without them these rules do not apply.","mistake":"Using parallel line rules when the lines are not marked parallel."}],"exam_tips":["Trace the F, Z and C shapes on the diagram to decide which rule applies.","Name the rule in your answer, the reason usually carries its own mark."],"related_topic_codes":["t11"],"order_index":903,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","created_at":"2026-07-28T07:20:22.476Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T07:20:22.476Z"},{"id":"019fa798-94cd-7126-b8a2-f1c4cb68dab4","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-78ab-b1d6-52be9d287151","subtopic_name":"Properties of quadrilaterals","summary":"Each special quadrilateral has its own set of side, angle and diagonal properties, and naming questions turn on the diagonals.","key_concepts":["A square has four equal sides, four right angles, and diagonals that are equal and bisect at right angles","A rectangle has equal diagonals that bisect each other, but not at right angles","A rhombus has four equal sides and diagonals that bisect at right angles but are unequal","A parallelogram has opposite sides equal and parallel and opposite angles equal","A kite has two pairs of adjacent equal sides, and one diagonal bisects the other at right angles"],"formulas":[{"note":"True for every quadrilateral.","label":"Angle sum of a quadrilateral","expression":"a + b + c + d = 360 degrees"},{"note":"a and b are the parallel sides, h the perpendicular height between them.","label":"Trapezium area","expression":"area = 1/2 (a + b) h"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Diagonals crossing at right angles rules out the rectangle and the plain parallelogram","Equal diagonals would make it a square, but here they are unequal","The remaining shape with these properties is a rhombus"],"answer":"A rhombus","question":"A quadrilateral has diagonals that bisect each other at right angles but are not equal in length. Name it and justify your answer."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"A rhombus has diagonals that bisect at right angles but are different lengths. Equal diagonals means a square or rectangle.","mistake":"Saying a rhombus has equal diagonals."},{"fix":"Only use properties that are marked or stated in the question.","mistake":"Assuming a shape is a square because it looks like one."},{"fix":"Compare them on three checks: equal sides, right angles, and what the diagonals do.","mistake":"Mixing up rhombus, rectangle and parallelogram properties."}],"exam_tips":["Build a table of the six quadrilaterals against sides, angles and diagonals, and learn it.","For naming questions, quote the property that rules out the other shapes."],"related_topic_codes":["t13"],"order_index":904,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","created_at":"2026-07-28T07:20:22.476Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T07:20:22.476Z"},{"id":"019fa798-94cd-7323-b7a3-4c838289aef8","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-78ab-b1d6-52be9d287151","subtopic_name":"Perpendicular and angle bisector constructions","summary":"Two ruler-and-compass constructions come up regularly: the perpendicular bisector of a line and the bisector of an angle.","key_concepts":["Every point on a perpendicular bisector is the same distance from both end points","Every point on an angle bisector is the same distance from both arms of the angle","Construction arcs must be left visible because they show the method","Set the compass to more than half the line length so the arcs actually cross"],"formulas":[{"note":"Cuts the line in half at 90 degrees.","label":"Perpendicular bisector","expression":"equal arcs from both end points, then join the crossing points"},{"note":"Splits the angle into two equal halves.","label":"Angle bisector","expression":"one arc across both arms, then equal arcs from those two points"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Open the compass to more than half of AB","Draw arcs above and below the line from A, then repeat from B with the same radius","Join the two points where the pairs of arcs cross"],"answer":"The line drawn is the perpendicular bisector of AB, which is the required locus","question":"Describe how to construct the locus of points equidistant from two points A and B."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"The arcs show your method and carry marks. Leave them on the page.","mistake":"Rubbing out the construction arcs to tidy up the diagram."},{"fix":"Keep the same radius for each pair of arcs.","mistake":"Changing the compass width partway through a construction."},{"fix":"Construct means ruler and compasses only.","mistake":"Measuring with a protractor when the question says construct."}],"exam_tips":["Use a sharp pencil and draw the arcs long enough to cross clearly.","Equidistant from two points means perpendicular bisector; equidistant from two lines means angle bisector."],"related_topic_codes":["t14"],"order_index":905,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","created_at":"2026-07-28T07:20:22.476Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T07:20:22.476Z"},{"id":"019fa77f-0ed2-7889-a1bc-441d9ff8f55c","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-78c7-aa4b-565799c65ce4","subtopic_name":"Congruence and similarity","summary":"Congruent triangles are the same shape and size. Similar triangles have the same shape with corresponding sides in proportion.","key_concepts":["Congruence tests: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, RHS (state the test used)","Similarity tests: AAA (two equal angles suffice), SSS sides proportional, SAS sides proportional with included equal angle","Congruent figures are identical in shape and size; similar figures share shape but not necessarily size"],"formulas":[{"note":"Match corresponding sides carefully.","label":"Length scale factor","expression":"k = corresponding length on larger / corresponding length on smaller"},{"note":"Square or cube the length factor for similar figures.","label":"Area and volume scaling","expression":"area ratio = k^2; volume ratio = k^3"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Two corresponding sides equal with the included angle equal","This is SAS congruence"],"answer":"SAS","question":"State which congruence rule applies when two triangles have two equal sides and the included equal angle."},{"steps":["Length scale factor k = 10 / 4 = 2.5","Volume scale factor = k^3 = 15.625","Larger volume = 32 x 15.625 = 500"],"answer":"500 cm^3","question":"Two similar solids have heights 4 cm and 10 cm. The smaller has volume 32 cm^3. Find the volume of the larger."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"AAA proves similarity, not congruence; sizes may differ.","mistake":"Claiming congruence from AAA alone."},{"fix":"Square it for area and cube it for volume.","mistake":"Using the length scale factor directly for area or volume."}],"exam_tips":["Sketch both triangles the same way round before pairing sides.","In proofs, name the triangles in corresponding vertex order and state the test (e.g. SAS)."],"related_topic_codes":["t13"],"order_index":1001,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","created_at":"2026-07-28T06:52:29.778Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:52:29.778Z"},{"id":"019fa77f-0ed2-78b5-bca6-3887a60c34d2","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-78da-b367-27466579928e","subtopic_name":"Circle properties and theorems","summary":"A short list of circle theorems covers nearly every question. Identify which one the diagram is showing before calculating.","key_concepts":["The angle in a semicircle is a right angle","A tangent meets a radius at 90 degrees","Angles in the same segment are equal"],"formulas":[{"note":"Both must stand on the same arc.","label":"Angle at the centre","expression":"angle at centre = 2 x angle at circumference"},{"note":"All four vertices must lie on the circle.","label":"Cyclic quadrilateral","expression":"opposite angles add to 180 degrees"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Angle ACB = 90 degrees, angle in a semicircle","Angles in triangle ABC sum to 180","Angle ABC = 180 - 90 - 34"],"answer":"56 degrees","question":"A, B and C lie on a circle with AB a diameter. Angle BAC is 34 degrees. Find angle ABC."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"The centre angle is the larger one. It is double the circumference angle.","mistake":"Halving the wrong angle in the centre and circumference theorem."},{"fix":"Check all four vertices lie on the circumference first.","mistake":"Applying the cyclic quadrilateral rule when a vertex is not on the circle."}],"exam_tips":["Look for the diameter first, it usually signals a right angle.","Name the theorem you used, the reason often carries its own mark."],"related_topic_codes":["t09"],"order_index":1101,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","created_at":"2026-07-28T06:52:29.778Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:52:29.778Z"},{"id":"019fa780-0e84-7e60-b2fc-65a592509a11","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-78eb-97ed-a2f26cb15634","subtopic_name":"Pythagoras and right-angled trigonometry","summary":"In a right-angled triangle, use Pythagoras for three sides and SOHCAHTOA when an angle is involved.","key_concepts":["Hypotenuse is the longest side, opposite the right angle","Label opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse relative to the angle you are using","Use inverse sin/cos/tan to find an angle from two sides"],"formulas":[{"note":"c is the hypotenuse.","label":"Pythagoras theorem","expression":"a^2 + b^2 = c^2"},{"note":"Choose the ratio that uses the two sides you know.","label":"SOHCAHTOA","expression":"sin = O/H; cos = A/H; tan = O/A"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Known opposite and hypotenuse, so use sine","sin theta = 3/5 = 0.6","theta = inverse sin(0.6)"],"answer":"theta = 36.9 degrees (1 d.p.)","question":"In a right-angled triangle, opposite = 3, adjacent = 4, hypotenuse = 5. Find the angle theta opposite the side of length 3."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Pythagoras only relates three sides. Use trigonometry when an angle appears.","mistake":"Using Pythagoras when one of the given values is an angle."},{"fix":"Set the calculator to degrees before any trigonometry.","mistake":"Leaving the calculator in radian mode."}],"exam_tips":["Label O, A and H relative to your chosen angle before picking a ratio.","Check the hypotenuse is the longest side in your answer."],"related_topic_codes":["t13"],"order_index":1201,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","created_at":"2026-07-28T06:53:35.236Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:53:35.236Z"},{"id":"019fa780-0e85-70c4-877c-8f32e666862f","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-78eb-97ed-a2f26cb15634","subtopic_name":"Sine rule, cosine rule and bearings","summary":"For triangles without a right angle, choose the sine rule or cosine rule based on what you are given.","key_concepts":["Sine rule needs a matching side and opposite angle pair","Cosine rule is for two sides and the included angle, or all three sides","Bearings are measured clockwise from north as three digits"],"formulas":[{"note":"Use when you have a side and its opposite angle.","label":"Sine rule","expression":"a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C"},{"note":"A is the angle between sides b and c.","label":"Cosine rule","expression":"a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc cos A"},{"note":"C is the angle between sides a and b.","label":"Area of a triangle","expression":"area = 1/2 ab sin C"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Two sides and the included angle, so use the cosine rule","a^2 = 49 + 81 - 2(7)(9)cos 62","a^2 = 130 - 126 x 0.4695 = 70.85","a = square root of 70.85"],"answer":"a = 8.42 cm to 3 significant figures","question":"In triangle ABC, b = 7 cm, c = 9 cm and angle A = 62 degrees. Find a."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"That case needs the cosine rule, because no side and opposite angle pair is complete.","mistake":"Using the sine rule when you only know two sides and the angle between them."},{"fix":"Bearings use three digits, so write 045 degrees.","mistake":"Writing a bearing as 45 degrees."}],"exam_tips":["Check what you are given before choosing a rule, it decides the method.","For bearings, draw a north arrow at every point mentioned."],"related_topic_codes":["t15"],"order_index":1202,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","created_at":"2026-07-28T06:53:35.236Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:53:35.236Z"},{"id":"019fa799-85b9-76bf-98d8-05beca89012f","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-78eb-97ed-a2f26cb15634","subtopic_name":"Angles of elevation, depression and 3D problems","summary":"Elevation and depression turn real situations into right-angled triangles. In three dimensions, work one triangle at a time.","key_concepts":["An angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal and an angle of depression is measured down from it","The angle of elevation from A to B equals the angle of depression from B to A, because the horizontals are parallel","In a 3D problem, pick out one right-angled triangle at a time and redraw it flat","You often need Pythagoras on the base before using trigonometry on a vertical triangle"],"formulas":[{"note":"They are alternate angles between two parallel horizontal lines.","label":"Elevation and depression","expression":"angle of elevation = angle of depression"},{"note":"Find this first, then use it as the base of the vertical triangle.","label":"Base diagonal of a cuboid","expression":"d = sqrt(l^2 + w^2)"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["The angle of depression from the cliff equals the angle of elevation at the boat, so the triangle has a 25 degree angle at the boat","The 40 m cliff is opposite that angle and the distance d is adjacent","tan 25 = 40 / d","d = 40 / tan 25 = 40 / 0.4663"],"answer":"85.8 m to 3 significant figures","question":"From the top of a 40 m cliff the angle of depression of a boat is 25 degrees. Find the distance of the boat from the foot of the cliff."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Both elevation and depression are measured from the horizontal.","mistake":"Measuring the angle of depression from the vertical."},{"fix":"Transfer it to the bottom of the triangle as an equal angle of elevation, which is usually simpler.","mistake":"Using the depression angle directly as the angle inside the triangle at the top."},{"fix":"Redraw each right-angled triangle separately and flat before calculating.","mistake":"Trying to solve a 3D problem on the original solid."}],"exam_tips":["Sketch the horizontal dashed line first, then mark the elevation or depression angle from it.","In 3D questions, name the triangle you are working in before substituting."],"related_topic_codes":["t13"],"order_index":1203,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","created_at":"2026-07-28T07:21:24.153Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T07:21:24.153Z"},{"id":"019fa780-0e85-70f7-afe0-beb56ca779e6","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-78fc-bd9e-a40e9b4f9363","subtopic_name":"Area, perimeter and circles","summary":"Break composite shapes into simple ones, and keep track of which parts of the perimeter are actually included.","key_concepts":["Perimeter is a length, area is a squared unit","An arc is a fraction of the circumference given by its angle","Composite shapes are best split into rectangles, triangles and circle parts"],"formulas":[{"note":"Check whether you are given the radius or the diameter.","label":"Circle","expression":"circumference = 2 pi r, area = pi r^2"},{"note":"x is the angle at the centre in degrees.","label":"Arc length and sector area","expression":"arc = (x / 360) x 2 pi r, sector = (x / 360) x pi r^2"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Radius = 7 cm","Curved part = half of 2 pi x 7 = 7 pi = 21.99 cm","Add the straight diameter: 21.99 + 14"],"answer":"35.99 cm, about 36.0 cm","question":"Find the perimeter of a semicircle of diameter 14 cm."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"The perimeter is the curved arc plus the diameter.","mistake":"Forgetting the straight edge when finding a semicircle perimeter."},{"fix":"Halve the diameter before substituting into the formula.","mistake":"Using the diameter in place of the radius."}],"exam_tips":["Write the units on every answer, cm for perimeter and cm^2 for area.","Keep pi in your calculator rather than using 3.14 until the final step."],"related_topic_codes":["t10"],"order_index":1301,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","created_at":"2026-07-28T06:53:35.236Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:53:35.236Z"},{"id":"019fa780-0e85-7115-8248-b56954b32be6","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-78fc-bd9e-a40e9b4f9363","subtopic_name":"Volume and surface area of solids","summary":"Volume fills a solid, surface area covers it. Curved surface area is the part most often forgotten.","key_concepts":["Prism volume is always cross-sectional area times length","Cones and pyramids include a factor of one third","Total surface area means every face, including the base if it is closed"],"formulas":[{"note":"Add two circles for a closed cylinder.","label":"Cylinder","expression":"volume = pi r^2 h, curved surface = 2 pi r h"},{"note":"l is the slant height, found with Pythagoras.","label":"Cone","expression":"volume = 1/3 pi r^2 h, curved surface = pi r l"},{"note":"A hemisphere is half the volume plus a flat circle.","label":"Sphere","expression":"volume = 4/3 pi r^3, surface area = 4 pi r^2"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Volume = 1/3 pi r^2 h","= 1/3 x pi x 9 x 8","= 24 pi"],"answer":"75.4 cm^3 to 3 significant figures","question":"Find the volume of a cone of radius 3 cm and vertical height 8 cm."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Volume uses the vertical height. Slant height is only for curved surface area.","mistake":"Using the slant height in the cone volume formula."},{"fix":"Any solid that tapers to a point needs the one third factor.","mistake":"Omitting the one third for cones and pyramids."}],"exam_tips":["Decide whether the solid is open or closed before totalling surface area.","Volume answers use cubic units, surface area uses squared units."],"related_topic_codes":["t12"],"order_index":1302,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","created_at":"2026-07-28T06:53:35.236Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:53:35.236Z"},{"id":"019fa780-0e85-712d-a090-4b3d82b18a9b","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-790d-b90f-3e453f40cd4c","subtopic_name":"Coordinate geometry","summary":"The Cartesian plane uses perpendicular x- and y-axes meeting at the origin (0, 0). Points, midpoints and distances are the basic tools.","key_concepts":["A point is written (x, y); the origin is (0, 0)","Read scales carefully: each small square may represent 1 unit or a fraction of a unit","Distance between two points comes from Pythagoras on the coordinate differences","Midpoint is the average of the x-coordinates and of the y-coordinates"],"formulas":[{"note":"Average each coordinate separately.","label":"Midpoint","expression":"((x1 + x2)/2, (y1 + y2)/2)"},{"note":"Same as length of the line segment joining the points.","label":"Distance","expression":"sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2)"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["Left of the origin means negative x","Above the origin means positive y"],"answer":"(-4, 7)","question":"A point is 4 units left of the origin and 7 units above it. State its coordinates."},{"steps":["y difference = -9 - (-5) = -4; x difference = -1 - 3 = -4","Distance = sqrt((-4)^2 + (-4)^2) = sqrt(32) = 5.66 units (3 s.f.)"],"answer":"5.66 units (3 s.f.)","question":"Find the distance between A(3, -5) and B(-1, -9)."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"Midpoint means average: add and divide by two.","mistake":"Subtracting coordinates when finding a midpoint."},{"fix":"Check what each small square represents before reading coordinates.","mistake":"Misreading the grid scale when plotting or reading a point."}],"exam_tips":["Always label the x-axis and y-axis on sketches.","Plot points roughly to sanity-check distance and midpoint answers."],"related_topic_codes":["t05"],"order_index":1401,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","created_at":"2026-07-28T06:53:35.236Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:53:35.236Z"},{"id":"019fa780-0e85-714b-8123-58667f21b215","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-791f-bec6-372d238905de","subtopic_name":"Vectors in two dimensions","summary":"A vector has magnitude and direction. Add by the triangle/parallelogram law, and use column vectors for components.","key_concepts":["Vector AB means go from A to B; BA = -AB","Triangle law: AB + BC = AC; subtract by adding the negative","Parallel vectors are scalar multiples; collinear points have AB = k AC","Magnitude of column vector (x / y) is sqrt(x^2 + y^2)"],"formulas":[{"note":"For the column vector (x / y).","label":"Magnitude","expression":"|v| = sqrt(x^2 + y^2)"},{"note":"Destination minus start.","label":"Displacement","expression":"AB = position of B - position of A"}],"worked_examples":[{"steps":["|BA| = sqrt(8^2 + (-6)^2) = 10","Position of A - BA = position of B: (-9 / 2) - (8 / -6) = (-17 / 8), so B = (-17, 8)","(m / -3) = k(8 / -6); k = (-3)/(-6) = 1/2, so m = 4"],"answer":"|BA| = 10; B = (-17, 8); m = 4","question":"A is (-9, 2) and BA = (8 / -6). Find |BA|, the coordinates of B, and m if CD = (m / -3) is parallel to BA."}],"common_mistakes":[{"fix":"AB = b - a (end minus start).","mistake":"Writing AB as a - b when OA = a and OB = b."},{"fix":"Add the components first, then apply the magnitude formula.","mistake":"Adding magnitudes to get the magnitude of a sum."}],"exam_tips":["Draw arrows on the diagram for every vector you write down.","If two vectors are parallel, write one as k times the other and solve for k."],"related_topic_codes":["t12"],"order_index":1501,"level_band":null,"recommended_levels":null,"curriculum_stage":"O-Level","strand":null,"estimated_minutes":null,"revision_status":"published","created_at":"2026-07-28T06:53:35.236Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T06:53:35.236Z"},{"id":"019fa780-0e85-71ab-b016-3c60cee766c0","topic_id":"019f9df7-a2a2-7930-a717-cd252273c91f","subtopic_name":"Averages and measures of spread","summary":"Mean, median and mode summarise a data set differently.
